questions.q: Why can't dbt itself be the tool that gets the marketing platform's CSV export into Snowflake?
options: dbt's job starts from data already inside Snowflake — every model reads from source() or ref(), never from a file sitting on a laptop
dbt requires a paid license to read external files
dbt does not support any file format other than Parquet
dbt only works with CSV files, never with database tables
questions.explain: Getting a brand-new external file into Snowflake in the first place is upstream of anything dbt does — that's the real gap Chapter 5 closes.

questions.q: Which two Python libraries does this chapter introduce for the ingestion job, and what is each one's role?
options: snowflake-connector-python for cleaning and pandas for connecting
NumPy for math and Flask for a web server
pandas for reading and cleaning the CSV, and snowflake-connector-python for connecting to and loading into Snowflake
Django for the ingestion app and pandas for scheduling
questions.explain: pandas handles reading/cleaning (pd.read_csv, dropna, type fixes); snowflake-connector-python handles the actual connection and load.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say snowflake-connector-python is introduced "honestly" as new ground?
options: Because this path's own Python course doesn't cover it specifically, so it's genuinely new material, introduced the same way any new real tool shows up mid-career
Because it's a fictional, made-up library for teaching purposes only
Because it requires a different programming language entirely
Because it was deprecated and replaced before this lesson was written
questions.explain: The lesson is upfront that this specific library wasn't covered earlier in the path, rather than pretending it was already familiar.

questions.q: Why is a "one-off CSV with no native connector" described as a realistic scenario rather than a contrived one?
options: Because Snowflake refuses to support any file-based ingestion
Because no real company has ever encountered this situation
Because real companies constantly accumulate exactly this kind of source — a vendor export, a partner's manual file drop, a legacy system with no modern API
Because CSV files are technically incapable of being loaded any other way
questions.explain: This is a deliberately common real-world pattern a production-grade platform has to have an answer for, not an edge case invented for the lesson.

questions.q: Which layer of the five-layer architecture from Lesson 2 does this Python ingestion chapter represent?
options: Layer 1 — Snowflake
Layer 3 — sitting between Snowflake and dbt
Layer 5 — Power BI
It doesn't correspond to any layer in that architecture
questions.explain: Python ingestion is Layer 3: it loads into the RAW schema Snowflake (Layer 1) already provides, and dbt (Layer 2) later builds staging models on top of what it lands.
